text:
lina: Quick alert — PolarisDocs onboarding showed a p95 latency regression after last night's model pin. p95 ~2.7s (baseline ~1.0s). Traffic is ~80% short chat, 18% medium, 2% long. No errors but customer flagged slowdown; renewal conversation coming next month so we should be proactive.

chris: Can you paste dashboard + token distro and any recent traffic changes?

lina: Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/polarisdocs/onboard-latency
lina: Token distro: short (<80) = 80%, medium (80-512) = 18%, long (>512) = 2%. Spike aligns with a recent partner integration that bumped concurrent requests.

emily: TL;DR: looks like batching interaction with larger model. Proposed proactive plan to avoid churn risk: 1) short-chat traffic route 7% -> redwood-compact-13b-int4 canary, 2) enable prefix/KV cache for short route (TTL 25s), 3) reduce max_batch_wait_ms for short route to 5ms, 4) instrument client feedback form + add renewal-note in CRM so CS team can capture sentiment.

jason: Risk summary:
- Model swap: risk=low-medium (edge-case semantics). Mitigation=rolling canary + 12-prompt eval set + quick accept criteria.
- Cache: risk=medium (stale prefix if they use dynamic system prompts). Mitigation=short TTL + mismatch metric + quick disable.
- Batching change: risk=medium (throughput drop). Mitigation=burst autoscale + monitor queue length and latency.

emily: I'll prep the eval set and the customer comms. Lina, can you own the canary and CS handoff? We should also capture their feedback post-canary and flag any negative phrasing in renewal notes.

lina: Yup — Ill run the canary and add a renewal note: "Investigating short-chat latency; running non-invasive canary to improve p95." Will include a 1-question feedback link in the app for negative experiences.

chris: Route rule snippet (draft). We'll gate by token_count to keep the change targeted:

```yaml
route: /v1/chat/completions
canary_percent: 7
route_rules:
  - match: "token_count < 80"
    model: redwood-compact-13b-int4
    overrides:
      batching:
        max_batch_wait_ms: 5
        max_batch_tokens: 2048
      cache:
        prefix_cache: true
        ttl_ms: 25000
fallback_policy:
  on_p95_breach: revert_after_consecutive: 3
```

chris: Eval gate: 12 prompts covering critical flows; abort if semantic similarity drops >2.5% or user-facing correctness regressions observed. Also ask client to add tiny client-side retry (200ms jitter).

emily: I'll prep the 1-question feedback text: "Did you notice slowness? (Yes / No) — optional comment" and wire results to CS dashboard. That way we can correlate objective metrics with customer sentiment for the renewal team.

lina: Deploy-bot — schedule a short 15m canary window at 09:45 UTC. Owner=lina.

deploy-bot: Canary scheduled: start=5102025150 (09:45 UTC), duration=15m, route=/v1/chat/completions, percent=7, owner=lina. Command: `/canary start --route /v1/chat/completions --model redwood-compact-13b-int4 --percent 7 --duration 15m --match token_count<80`

jason: I'll enable tracing on top-3 endpoints and add autoscale guard for the pool. Also will add a quick renewal-risk tag if CS reports any negative feedback within 24h.

lina: Notifying PolarisDocs: "We will run a brief 15-minute canary at 09:45 UTC to test a compact model + caching on short-chat traffic. No downtime expected; we will share p50/p95, KV hit-rate, and feedback summary. If any regression, we will revert immediately." :thumbsup:

emily: I'll monitor sentiment/feedback and add notes to the renewal tracker. If we see two or more negative feedback items within 24h, we escalate to AMs.

chris: Monitoring p50/p95, queue lengths, KV hit rate, eval results. If anything crosses thresholds, we abort and revert.

lina: Thanks team — will post canary outcome in this thread within 30 minutes after end (p50/p95, KV hit %, eval delta, and feedback count)"
